result.title: ADAPT for Science: A Multi-Agent System for Self-Evolving Scientific Optimization
result.summary: Scientific discovery often requires identifying a small number of high-performing designs in vast, constrained search spaces. This is difficult when evaluations are costly, feasible solutions are sparse, parameters are strongly coupled, and physical constraints are strict. Recent AI for AI methods can automatically improve algorithms and optimization procedures. However, general purpose approaches are not designed around scientific priors, physical constraints, and limited evaluation budgets. We introduce ADAPT for Science, a multi-agent framework that treats scientific optimization as two coupled decisions: where to search and how to search. ADAPT uses historical designs to identify promising and diverse initial conditions, progressively concentrates computation on favorable search directions, and evolves the optimization procedure from execution feedback. We evaluate ADAPT on the design of gravitational wave detectors using a differentiable physics simulator and eight unseen detector topologies. Under matched scientific evaluation budgets, ADAPT achieves a mean loss of 0.204 +/- 0.101, reducing loss by 54.9% relative to the best classical optimizer and by 62.2% relative to the best general purpose agentic evolution baseline. ADAPT achieves the lowest loss on all unseen topologies among the evaluated baselines. ADAPT provides a step toward scientific optimization systems that continuously learn from prior experience and their own search outcomes.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 ADAPT for Science 多智能体框架，将科学优化拆为「在哪搜索」与「如何搜索」两个耦合决策：借助历史设计给出有前景且多样的初始条件，逐步把计算集中到有利搜索方向，并由执行反馈演化优化流程，在引力波探测器设计中验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其依据反馈渐进收缩计算、并演化搜索过程的方法线索，可能为 LVR 中的动态计算分配、搜索与停止决策提供可供核查的借鉴，但任务域与视觉推理相距较远，需较多核查。
